name: Mission Control

features.title: Calendar
features.summary: See your day without hopping between windows.
features.why: Useful if appointments shape your day. Start with a read-only agenda or week view. Editing and dragging are separate choices.
steps: Choose agenda or week layout and the calendars to display. Begin with read access; ask separately about creating or moving events.
Adapt EventKit reads and the timeline into an independent Calendar service. Add the selected access-purpose description and stable app signing. Request access only when the owner connects Calendar.
Distinguish unavailable access from a genuinely empty day. Preserve timezones, all-day dates and recurrence occurrences.
If writes are selected, adapt exact target/revision checks, persistent operation receipts and fresh readback. Never write by matching a title.
acceptance: Denied access shows an unavailable state without inventing an empty day.
All-day and timed events render correctly across timezone and daylight-saving boundaries.
If editing is selected, a disposable approved event moves once and readback confirms its exact values; interrupted saves are not replayed.
features.permissions: Calendar permission for the selected capability. No Reminders or Mail permission is implied.

features.title: Apple Reminders
features.summary: Bring your existing to-dos into your space.
features.why: Useful if Apple Reminders already holds your personal tasks. These are native reminders; Project tasks are a different, optional kind of record.
steps: Choose lists and whether the first version can only read, or can also create/complete reminders on explicit requests.
Adapt the reminder service into its own selected source. Add its usage description and permission request at connection time.
Retain list IDs, date-only versus timed due dates, completion state and recurrence semantics. Do not convert date-only reminders into midnight appointments.
For selected writes, issue exact current identities, validate captured fields, save a pending receipt and verify by readback. Expose supported Undo honestly.
acceptance: Permission denial and an empty list remain distinct.
Completing an approved fictional/disposable reminder changes only that exact record.
Date-only and recurring reminders survive reopen with the same intended date and scope.
features.permissions: Reminders permission. Calendar and Projects are not required.

features.title: Projects & notes
features.summary: Give longer work a home, with tasks and notes together.
features.why: Useful for work that spans days or weeks: a project, a side business, an application or a creative idea. It works without Apple accounts.
steps: Start with local spaces, tasks and notes. Choose a simple list, board or both. Use the foundation account/storage identity.
Adapt the workspace model and persistence before mounting views. Keep IDs and hierarchy stable; separate Project tasks from Apple Reminders.
Expose only selected project tools to the assistant. The human owns project creation and changes; mentioning an idea in chat does not automatically create a project.
Add reversible local edits and exact parent/revision checks. Preserve folder defaults, ordering and recently deleted identities.
acceptance: A space, child task and note reopen under the same account and identities.
A second account cannot see or mutate the first account's project records.
Moving a task, undoing and restoring a deleted item preserve its intended parent and ID.
features.permissions: Local app storage only. No Calendar, Reminders or external account is required.

features.title: Review inbox
features.summary: Consider useful suggestions and choose what happens next.
features.why: Useful if you want an assistant to prepare possible next steps for you to inspect. A saved suggestion can have a conversation, a checkbox plan and a clear result.
steps: Choose the kinds of suggestions to prepare and their actual sources. Manual generation is a valid first version; heartbeat is optional.
Create a persistent inbox with exact proposal identities, action payloads, selection state and outcomes. Reading saved cards must not start AI work.
Separate proposal creation from approving displayed concrete actions. Apply only the selected exact actions under the current source/account and destination permissions.
Adapt canonical receipts, duplicate grouping, never-started job recovery and outcome display. Uncertain or interrupted writes require outcome checking rather than blind replay.
acceptance: Opening the inbox displays saved cards with zero inference requests.
Approving a selected concrete action executes it once and shows a verified result.
Dismiss/Undo, reopen and duplicate proposals retain their expected state; an uncertain save cannot be replayed automatically.
features.permissions: Depends on the chosen suggestion source and action destination. Email, Projects and heartbeat are possible companions, not mandatory bundles.

features.title: Heartbeat
features.summary: Let your space check in at times you choose.
features.why: Useful when you want recurring briefs or suggestions. It performs selected AI work over available inputs; it does not mean every source is connected.
steps: Agree the actual jobs, interval, notification style and usage expectations. Leave automatic work off until the owner chooses it.
Start with one selected job, such as updating a brief. Adapt durable due-time/run state and the power gate without importing every 3PO learning/review lane.
Keep source collection separate. A heartbeat consumes permitted collected snapshots; a source refresh alone makes no AI request.
Retain serial ownership, Stop, usage pause, sleep/closed-lid/dark-wake checks and one catch-up after full wake. Avoid replaying every missed interval or retrying failed personal actions.
acceptance: A fictional clock produces one due run and no run while disabled or already busy.
Sleep interruption preserves due state; full wake catches up once without a retry storm.
A failed selected lane preserves completed outcomes and schedules a fresh future cycle.
Perform a real sleep/wake acceptance check separately before claiming ordinary-use reliability.
features.permissions: Recurring model usage, explicitly enabled by the owner. Only the selected jobs and sources are started.

features.title: Context & memory
features.summary: Keep useful background available without repeating yourself.
features.why: Useful for background you want the assistant to retain: ongoing work, your preferred routines or the meaning of a project. It is distinct from chat history.
steps: Choose explicit human-owned notes first or AI-maintained context pages. Automatic learning and periodic consolidation are separate opt-ins.
Use the current page-first 3PO implementation. Ordinary chat receives a small guide and relevant pages/working changes; avoid reviving the older parallel raw-fact feed.
Preserve canonical evidence, corrections/history, source/account ownership and exact identity. Feature instructions remain distinct from factual background.
Add inspect, edit, correct and forget controls. If sources or Projects are selected, use their exact access/identity contracts rather than silently importing all data.
acceptance: The owner can inspect what was supplied to a reply and correct or forget a specific piece of background.
Another account and unpermitted source evidence cannot enter recall.
No page learning runs merely because its view opens; selected consolidation is separately controlled.
Verify relevant context is used without automatically injecting all stored facts.
features.permissions: Local records and selected model context. Learning from conversations or external sources requires its own chosen controls.

features.title: Read-only Mail
features.summary: Bring relevant messages into view, with drafts you control.
features.why: Useful if incoming messages influence your work. Start with selected accounts and read-only lookup. Assessment, drafts and Review are additional choices.
steps: Choose Apple Mail accounts and whether the app may show headers, read bodies or send selected content to inference for the chosen purpose.
Adapt read-only collection and bounded lookup. Request Mail Automation only when connecting. Keep collection and model interpretation separate.
Use incremental per-account identity/cursor coverage and backoff; a body-read failure must not stop every account or imply there is no mail.
If drafts are selected, keep them local for review/edit/copy. Do not add sending, mark-read or other Mail writes. Add Review or heartbeat only if the owner chooses those features.
acceptance: Collection makes no inference requests and preserves Mail read/unread state.
Unavailable accounts are labelled unavailable; partial history is not presented as complete.
A selected lookup respects account boundaries, stops promptly and never sends a reply.
Draft text stays local until the person copies or separately handles it.
features.permissions: Apple Mail Automation and selected account/purpose controls. Mail is read-only in the reference implementation.

features.title: Read-only WhatsApp
features.summary: Include selected conversations in your own workspace.
features.why: Useful if selected personal conversations provide relevant context. This optional connector uses an unofficial linked-device helper and can break or face restrictions.
steps: Explain the linked-device approach and confirm the owner wants it. Let them scan their own QR code and choose chats; never reuse another app's session.
Adapt the separate helper package, pinned runtime packaging and encrypted session/message/name storage. Give the new app its own helper/storage/Keychain identities.
Keep chat selection and AI-purpose permissions explicit. Reception may cache unselected text; explain this distinction instead of promising selection limits reception.
Keep the helper read-only: no sending, presence changes or read-receipt commands. Stop it when disconnected; do not silently relink or expand chats.
acceptance: The owner completes linking and the selected chat list matches their choice.
Fictional helper tests reject write/read-receipt/presence commands.
Account changes and disconnection invalidate old source access; local sessions stay separate from 3PO.
Missing or partial history is labelled honestly.
features.permissions: Optional unofficial Baileys helper, Node/npm during preparation and human QR consent. No other source is required.

features.title: Weather
features.summary: A little local context for planning the day.
features.why: Useful if travel, a walk or outdoor plans change with the forecast. Add it as a small standalone view or as optional brief context.
steps: Let the owner choose a manual location or optional location permission. Do not infer an address from unrelated personal records.
Adapt the weather service and cache with its own explicit refresh. Weather refresh need not invoke the assistant.
Show location, forecast date/time and cached/stale state. Include weather in briefs only when current data is actually supplied.
acceptance: A fixture forecast renders dates, units and location correctly.
Unavailable or stale weather is labelled and never fabricated by the model.
Refreshing weather triggers no AI request.
features.permissions: Network forecast access; location permission only if selected. Check the current forecast provider terms and attribution before distribution.

features.title: MCP & other integrations
features.summary: Connect another useful tool when you have a reason to.
features.why: Useful when your chosen workflow needs a service beyond the supplied examples. Start with the actual task, then decide whether native code, a direct API or MCP is appropriate.
steps: Identify the service, intended read/write operations, supported authentication and where its connector will run.
Distinguish the coding assistant's tools from the finished app's runtime. A plugin installed in Claude/Codex does not install it into a new app.
Implement a local client/adapter for the chosen service. The 3PO tool protocol/session illustrates typed execution boundaries, not a complete generic MCP client.
Expose only selected tools, validate schemas/owners/capabilities and keep secrets in an appropriate credential store. For writes, add exact authority, durable receipts and saved-outcome verification.
Check current service and MCP documentation, and the ChatGPT subscription route's supported tools. Do not assume provider-hosted connectors are available.
acceptance: Only selected tools appear in the app's actual runtime tool list.
Revoked/expired authorization and unavailable services produce clear bounded failures.
Read-only tools cannot dispatch writes. Approved writes are verified and uncertain results are not replayed.
The app works when the developer's coding assistant is closed.
features.permissions: Depends on the chosen service. This recipe is guidance for new integration work, not a prebuilt MCP module.

features.title: Your dashboard
features.summary: Arrange the information you want to see.
features.why: Useful when several selected features deserve their own panels. Start with a fixed tidy layout, then add movable/resizable widgets or multiple pages if wanted.
steps: Ask which selected features should be visible together. Retain default spacing, typography and colours unless the owner asks for another style.
Adapt saved pages/widget identities and layout geometry independently from source services. Adding a panel must not implicitly connect its source.
Mount only selected widget kinds. Preserve layout state across edits, resize and reopening; an absent feature must not start a hidden service.
Support keyboard navigation, readable contrast and light/dark appearance. Choose whether saved themes and drag editing are needed in the first version.
acceptance: Reordering/resizing and reopening retain the layout and stable IDs.
Showing, hiding and editing a widget do not change source permissions or create AI requests.
Narrow windows, long titles and light/dark modes remain usable.
features.permissions: Local appearance/layout storage. Individual widgets use only the permissions of their selected feature.

previewDisclosure: Illustrative preview with fictional content. Layouts vary; optional features need integration.
